state.misconception_label: Believes f(x - a) translates the function up a units

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: What transformation maps the graph of \(y=f(x) \) to the graph of \( y=f(x-3) \). I got Translation by vector
\(
\left[\begin{array}{l}
0 \\
3
\end{array}\right]
\) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Imagine you have a function that represents the height of a ball thrown into the air. If you shift the function \(f(x)\) to \(f(x-3)\), think about how that would change the ball's trajectory. How would the ball's position be affected by the shift of 3 units to the right? This analogy might help you better understand the concept of translating a function.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I think I get what you're saying about the ball. So if I move the function to the right, it would actually be like the ball starting 3 units later, right? But I'm still confused about why that means the translation is by \(\left[\begin{array}{l} 0 \\ 3 \end{array}\right]\). Shouldn't it be something else since it's moving right?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Think about it this way: when we shift the function to the right by 3 units, we're actually replacing \(x\) with \(x-3\). Just like in the misconceptions about solving for \(x\) in a linear or quadratic equation, we need to be careful about how we adjust the variables. So, in this case, the translation by \(\left[\begin{array}{l} 0 \\ 3 \end{array}\right]\) represents the shift up by 3 units, not to the right.
